summary: Frontend-only validation completed on public preview for menu language-switch hiding, hero lifecycle behavior, EastWest border lifecycle, and header logo/preload consistency. Chromium automation passed key interaction checks. Existing lang-toggle regression suite has 2 outdated assertions vs newly requested markup/animation scope.

integration_issues.flow: Hero video progression on project pages in automation runner
integration_issues.issue: In Chromium screenshot runner, 6 project hero pages reported currentTime 0.00->0.00 while homepage and ANA pages progressed. Pause persistence and resume hooks still passed. This is likely runner codec/decode capability mismatch, not confirmed app regression.

Could not execute independent WebKit automation in this environment because both Python and Node Playwright packages are unavailable for direct runner scripts (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND / ModuleNotFoundError).

action_items: Update /app/tests/test_lang_toggle_regression.py expectations/fixture scope: current assertions still require non-language HTML/CSS byte identity, which conflicts with newly requested header preload and EastWest animation refactor changes.
If strict cross-browser verification is mandatory, run the same lifecycle suite in an environment with standalone Playwright runtimes (Chromium + WebKit) installed.
Optional: validate project-page hero decoding on physical Safari/iOS and Android Chrome before classifying project-page 0.00->0.00 in automation as product regression.
critical_code_review_comments: runtime_markup.py now injects one header preload and standardized eager/sync/high logo attrs correctly across all 66 pages (validated via public endpoint tests).
Menu-open language hiding behavior is correctly gated by <=1100 breakpoint; desktop 1440/1920 remains visible as required.
EastWest border implementation is WAAPI transform-based and lifecycle-pauses/resumes correctly in Chromium automation checks.
test_lang_toggle_regression.py currently enforces a pre-change invariant (only lang-switch diffs allowed), which is no longer compatible with this feature scope and causes false failures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Executed pytest: static_pages + i18n_serving_modes + lang_toggle_regression => 163 pass, 2 fail (both in outdated lang-toggle strictness checks); header asset suite => 66/66 pass. Chromium automation confirmed menu hide/show behavior at 320/390/768/1024/1100/1440/1920, hero pause persistence + nova:hero-resume on all 12 pages, and EastWest border progress/pause/resume. Could not run standalone WebKit automation due missing direct Playwright runtime packages in this environment. Physical iOS app-switch was NOT tested.
rca of the issue: Regression failures are test-baseline mismatches, not confirmed product breakage. Root cause: /app/tests/test_lang_toggle_regression.py still asserts full non-lang byte identity and CSS-prefix identity against old baseline, but current approved scope intentionally changed non-lang markup/CSS (header preload/logo attrs and EastWest border implementation). Mitigation: update fixture/snapshot to constrained new scope and keep semantic checks (link attrs, active language state) instead of whole-file byte locks.
